title: Long Conversation — Detailed History and Multiple Areas
description: Extended intake covering detailed personal history, treatment history, and complex family context

conversation.content: Thank you for coming. What brings you here today?
I've been struggling with low mood for most of my adult life, but it's been worse in the last year since I changed jobs.
Tell me more about the low mood. How does it present for you day to day?
I feel hopeless a lot of the time. I don't enjoy things I used to. I used to love painting but I haven't touched it in six months.
You mentioned this has been part of your life for a long time — has this ever been treated before?
Yes. I saw a therapist for two years in my mid-twenties — that was helpful. I was also on sertraline for about a year but I stopped it because of side effects.
What side effects did you experience with the medication?
Mostly nausea and feeling emotionally flat. My doctor knew I stopped.
Are you taking any medications currently?
Just a vitamin D supplement. Nothing else.
How about family — is there any history of mental health concerns in your family?
My father struggled with alcohol for years. My sister had a breakdown in her thirties — she's doing well now though.
How is your current support system?
I have a partner who is supportive but doesn't fully understand what I go through. I have a few close friends but I don't talk to them about this much.
How are things like sleep, appetite, and energy?
Sleep is very disrupted — about 5 hours with a lot of waking. Appetite varies. Energy is low most days but I still manage my responsibilities.
Have you ever had thoughts of harming yourself?
Years ago, yes. Not currently. I feel motivated to get better — I'm getting married next year and I want to be well for that.
What are you hoping to get from support?
To understand this pattern better and develop better coping strategies. I'm open to therapy and possibly medication again if it's the right fit.
